name: South Korea
summary: South Korea has no officially reserved example values of any kind: no identifiers, phone numbers or example domains (example.kr and example.co.kr are registered). Its e-tax invoice uses the KEC XML standard, not UBL, and Korea has no Peppol authority. The common "example" business registration number 123-45-67890 fails the check digit. A checksum-valid party-set series (000-81-0nnnC) was derived, but Korean registers could not be queried, so it is not listed as usable. Also not listed because unverified: postcodes 00xxx and 64xxx-99xxx (outside the range Korea Post says it assigned, but not checked against the postcode database) and mobile numbers 010-0xxx/010-1xxx (reportedly not assignable; not confirmed in the MSIT rules). What remains usable are the UPU address examples, the placeholder name 홍길동 and RFC 2606/6761 domains.

identifiers.name: Business registration number (사업자등록번호)
identifiers.format: 10 digits, written XXX-XX-XXXXX (tax office, type, serial, check digit)
identifiers.notes: Type digits 81 = for-profit corporation HQ, 85 = branch, 01–79 = individuals. Check digit = weights 1,3,7,1,3,7,1,3,5 on digits 1–9, plus floor(d₉ × 5 / 10), then (10 − sum mod 10) mod 10; algorithm from consistent secondary sources, no NTS primary document found.

identifiers.name: Corporate registration number (법인등록번호)
identifiers.notes: Check digit commonly described as weights 1,2,1,2,… then (10 − sum mod 10) mod 10; unverified.

identifiers.name: Resident registration number (주민등록번호)
identifiers.authority: Ministry of the Interior and Safety (행정안전부)
identifiers.notes: Since 5 October 2020 the six digits after the gender digit are random, so a checksum proves nothing. Collection restricted by the Personal Information Protection Act. Do not use.
